posts.name: Silverleaf
posts.cooked:
I have a large pan, a candy thermometer, and some oil.

I'm English, of course I can make chips! ;) My favourite way is triple-cooking them with a supplementary freezing step - parboil, fry at low temperature until cooked but not coloured, freeze overnight, then final fry from frozen. The ice crystals forming affects the structure of the potato and the final product is more crispy. Unnecessary, but good.

Curd cheese might be hard to source though, unless we call that something else over here.

posts.name: phantaskippy
posts.cooked:
It's the curd of the cheese before they make it into the cheese.

 

I get Mozzerella cheese curd from the Strip here, any place that sells fresh mazzerella should have cheese curd.

 

I've done that with fries, it's how McDonalds does their fries, and the result is great, works fantastic with poutine.

The gravy is a 1/2 chicken 1/2 beef gravy, it is a bit wierd, but if you google poutine gravy you should find one.

There's a great little microbrewery/restaurant south of Dayton--Lock 27--that does a spectacular poutine:  well-fried fries, great cheese curds, and beef braised in one of their own microbrews.  So good!

Better yet?  They're directly across the street from one of my favorite game stores, Epic Loot.  Makes for a great night out!
